notes.1: Close: both passages give a vapor pressure (butadiene 2 atm @15.3 C vs arsenic trichloride 10 mm Hg @23.5 C) and a boiling/freezing point, but of different substances; nothing can contradict anything.
notes.2: LPG container design-pressure table (psig) vs SPCC aggregate aboveground storage threshold (1,320 gal); unrelated subjects.
notes.3: Close: both use 'capacity' in gallons (oxygen 0-1000/1001 gal vs service-station closed containers <=60 gal), but one is oxygen storage, the other flammable liquids at service stations.
notes.5: Close: both passages use 'capacity' (2.5 L nitric-acid glass receptacles vs 1,200 gal movable fuel tenders) for entirely different containers.
notes.6: Rad/rem radiation dose units vs 1,3-butadiene sampling target concentration; no shared subject.
notes.7: Radiation dose units vs 49 CFR residual-material gauge pressure (<200 kPa / 29.0 psig); unrelated.
notes.8: Butadiene sampling target concentration (1 ppm) vs packaging residual gauge pressure (200 kPa); unrelated subjects.
notes.12: Butadiene vapor pressure vs PSM threshold quantity (10,000 lb / 4535.9 kg for a Category 1 flammable gas); different subjects.
notes.15: Close: 1,200 gal (OSHA limit on a movable fuel storage tender/farm cart, 1910.110) vs 1,320 gal (EPA aggregate aboveground oil storage exemption, 40 CFR 112). Different programs and different subjects; the SPCC rule even excludes motive power containers.
notes.18: Oxygen minimum-separation-by-capacity table vs LP-gas container marking paragraph; different commodities and different sections.
notes.21: Close: 'capacity' for a fuel tender (1,200 gal) vs oxygen capacity in cu ft NTP (5,000 cu ft); different subjects.
notes.22: Nitric-acid inner receptacle capacity (2.5 L) vs LP-gas container separation distances by water capacity; different subjects.
notes.25: Oxygen separation table vs 1910.110 definitions (PSIG/PSIA, ventilation at 25 percent of LFL); different subjects.
notes.31: Close: both passages use 'action level' and 'exposure', but formaldehyde (0.5 ppm AL, 2 ppm STEL) vs arsenic (5 ug/m3 AL) are different substances with different limits.
notes.35: Close: both tables give a minimum 'distance (feet)' keyed to a container 'capacity' in gallons, but one is oxygen (50/90 ft) and the other LP-gas (10-100 ft). Different commodities, different sections; the shared 50 ft is coincidental.
notes.36: Nitric-acid packaging capacity (2.5 L) vs grain terminal elevator permanent storage capacity (88,100 m3); different subjects.
notes.38: Both are 1910.110 on the same object: one states the required minimum design pressure of a container, the other states the required markings on that container. No competing value; compatible.
notes.44: Close: oxygen capacity thresholds (1,000/1,001 gal) vs SPCC aggregate storage (1,320 gal); different commodities and programs.
notes.48: Same SPCC programme (40 CFR 112): one passage is the response-plan submission obligation/date, the other the small-facility (1,320 gal) exemption. Complementary, no competing number.
notes.58: Same section 1910.110, but different subjects: the design-pressure table vs the definitions (PSIG/PSIA, systems, ventilation at 25 percent of LFL). Compatible but not the same measured property.
notes.60: SPCC response-plan obligation vs LP-gas container separation distances; different subjects.
